user_prompt: Create a systemd unit file for myapp

dm_json.name: myapp-unit-create
dm_json.code:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/{{input.service_name}}.service <<UNIT
[Unit]
Description={{input.description}}
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User={{input.run_user}}
ExecStart={{input.exec_start}}
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT
systemctl daemon-reload && echo "Unit file created and daemon reloaded"

service_name.description: Name for the new systemd service

run_user.description: User to run the service as

exec_start.description: Full path to the executable command

explanation: Creates a new systemd unit file for myapp with configurable user, description, and executable.

Unit={{input.timer_name}}.service

[Install]

user_prompt: Clean up zombie processes on the system

dm_json.name: system-zombie-cleanup
dm_json.code: ZOMBIES=$(ps aux | awk '$8=="Z" {print $2}'); if [ -z "$ZOMBIES" ]; then echo "No zombie processes found"; exit 0; fi; echo "Found zombie PIDs: $ZOMBIES"; for ZPID in $ZOMBIES; do PPID=$(ps -o ppid= -p "$ZPID" 2>/dev/null | tr -d " "); if [ -n "$PPID" ] && [ "$PPID" != "1" ]; then echo "Sending SIGCHLD to parent PID $PPID of zombie $ZPID"; kill -SIGCHLD "$PPID" 2>/dev/null; fi; done; sleep 1; REMAINING=$(ps aux | awk '$8=="Z"' | wc -l); echo "Zombie processes remaining: $REMAINING"

explanation: Finds zombie processes on the system and sends SIGCHLD to their parents to trigger cleanup.

expected_checksum.description: Expected SHA-256 checksum (leave empty to generate)

explanation: Verifies archive backup integrity by computing or comparing SHA-256 checksums.

user_prompt: Set up root login email alerts on the production

dm_json.name: production-root-login-alert
dm_json.code:
ALERT_SCRIPT="/usr/local/bin/root-login-alert.sh" && cat > "$ALERT_SCRIPT" <<'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
if [ "$PAM_USER" = "root" ] && [ "$PAM_TYPE" = "open_session" ]; then
  SUBJECT="Root login alert on $(hostname)"
  BODY="Root login detected\nUser: $PAM_USER\nRemote Host: $PAM_RHOST\nService: $PAM_SERVICE\nTime: $(date)\nTTY: $PAM_TTY"
  echo -e "$BODY" | mail -s "$SUBJECT" "ALERT_EMAIL"
fi
SCRIPT
sed -i "s/ALERT_EMAIL/{{input.alert_email}}/g" "$ALERT_SCRIPT" && chmod 755 "$ALERT_SCRIPT" && if ! grep -q "root-login-alert" /etc/pam.d/sshd; then echo "session optional pam_exec.so /usr/local/bin/root-login-alert.sh" >> /etc/pam.d/sshd; fi && echo "Root login email alert configured ({{input.alert_email}})"

alert_email.description: Email address to receive root login alerts

explanation: Configures a PAM-based email alert on the production that sends a notification whenever root logs in via SSH.

service_port.description: Port number to restrict access to

allowed_ips.description: Space-separated list of allowed IP addresses or CIDRs

user_prompt: Apply kernel parameter hardening on the node

dm_json.name: node-kernel-harden
dm_json.code:
SYSCTL_FILE="/etc/sysctl.d/99-hardening.conf" && cat > "$SYSCTL_FILE" <<SYSCTL
# Network hardening
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0
net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.default.send_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route = 0
net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians = 1
net.ipv4.conf.default.log_martians = 1
net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts = 1
net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies = 1
# Kernel hardening
kernel.randomize_va_space = 2
kernel.sysrq = 0
kernel.core_uses_pid = 1
fs.suid_dumpable = 0
SYSTL
sysctl -p "$SYSCTL_FILE" 2>&1 && echo "Kernel parameters hardened via $SYSCTL_FILE"

explanation: Applies kernel parameter hardening on the node including network, ASLR, and core dump protections via sysctl.

dm_json.code: EXPIRY_DATE=$(echo | openssl s_client -servername {{input.hostname}} -connect {{input.hostname}}:{{input.port}} 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -enddate 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2) && if [ -z "$EXPIRY_DATE" ]; then echo "FAILED: Could not retrieve certificate for {{input.hostname}}:{{input.port}}" >&2; exit 1; fi && EXPIRY_EPOCH=$(date -d "$EXPIRY_DATE" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -j -f "%b %d %T %Y %Z" "$EXPIRY_DATE" +%s 2>/dev/null) && NOW_EPOCH=$(date +%s) && DAYS_LEFT=$(( (EXPIRY_EPOCH - NOW_EPOCH) / 86400 )) && echo "Certificate for {{input.hostname}} expires: $EXPIRY_DATE ($DAYS_LEFT days remaining)" && if [ "$DAYS_LEFT" -le "{{input.critical_days}}" ]; then echo "CRITICAL: Certificate expires in $DAYS_LEFT days" >&2; exit 2; elif [ "$DAYS_LEFT" -le "{{input.warning_days}}" ]; then echo "WARNING: Certificate expires in $DAYS_LEFT days" >&2; exit 1; else echo "OK: Certificate is valid for $DAYS_LEFT more days"; fi

hostname.description: Hostname to check the SSL certificate for

warning_days.description: Warn if certificate expires within this many days

critical_days.description: Critical alert if certificate expires within this many days

explanation: Checks the SSL certificate expiry date for the vpn endpoint and alerts based on warning/critical thresholds.

user_prompt: Count errors in the nginx application log

dm_json.name: nginx-error-count
dm_json.code: if [ ! -f "{{input.log_file}}" ]; then echo "FAILED: Log file not found: {{input.log_file}}" >&2; exit 1; fi && ERROR_COUNT=$(grep -c -i "{{input.error_pattern}}" "{{input.log_file}}" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) && echo "Error count in {{input.log_file}}: $ERROR_COUNT (pattern: {{input.error_pattern}})" && if [ "$ERROR_COUNT" -ge "{{input.threshold}}" ]; then echo "CRITICAL: $ERROR_COUNT errors found (threshold: {{input.threshold}})" >&2; echo "=== Recent matching lines ===" && grep -i "{{input.error_pattern}}" "{{input.log_file}}" | tail -5; exit 1; else echo "OK: Error count ($ERROR_COUNT) is below threshold ({{input.threshold}})"; fi

log_file.description: Path to the application log file

error_pattern.description: Grep pattern to match errors (e.g. ERROR, FATAL, Exception)

lookback_minutes.description: Number of minutes to look back in the log

explanation: Counts error occurrences in the nginx application log and alerts if the count exceeds the threshold.

dm_json.code: certbot certonly --non-interactive --agree-tos --email {{input.email}} --{{input.challenge_type}} -d {{input.domain}} --cert-name {{input.cert_name}} 2>&1; RC=$?; if [ $RC -eq 0 ]; then echo "Certificate issued for {{input.domain}}" && ls -la /etc/letsencrypt/live/{{input.cert_name}}/ 2>&1 && openssl x509 -in /etc/letsencrypt/live/{{input.cert_name}}/fullchain.pem -noout -subject -dates 2>&1; elif [ $RC -eq 1 ]; then echo "FAILED: certbot error" >&2; exit 1; else echo "Certificate may already exist, checking..." && certbot certificates --cert-name {{input.cert_name}} 2>&1; fi

user_prompt: Check if the api certificate needs renewal

dm_json.name: api-cert-renewal
dm_json.code: if [ ! -f "{{input.cert_path}}" ]; then echo "FAILED: Certificate file not found: {{input.cert_path}}" >&2; exit 1; fi && EXPIRY=$(openssl x509 -in {{input.cert_path}} -noout -enddate 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2) && EXPIRY_EPOCH=$(date -d "$EXPIRY" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -j -f "%b %d %T %Y %Z" "$EXPIRY" +%s 2>/dev/null) && NOW_EPOCH=$(date +%s) && DAYS_LEFT=$(( (EXPIRY_EPOCH - NOW_EPOCH) / 86400 )) && SUBJECT=$(openssl x509 -in {{input.cert_path}} -noout -subject 2>/dev/null) && echo "Certificate: {{input.cert_path}}" && echo "Subject: $SUBJECT" && echo "Expires: $EXPIRY ($DAYS_LEFT days remaining)" && if [ "$DAYS_LEFT" -le "{{input.renew_days}}" ]; then echo "ACTION REQUIRED: Certificate needs renewal (threshold: {{input.renew_days}} days)" >&2; exit 1; else echo "OK: Certificate is valid, no renewal needed"; fi

cert_path.description: Path to the PEM certificate file to check

renew_days.description: Days before expiry to trigger renewal alert

import sys

req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="POST")

import json
import urllib.request
import time
import sys

url = "{{input.url}}"
max_retries = int("{{input.max_retries}}" or "30")
interval = int("{{input.interval}}" or "10")

for attempt in range(1, max_retries + 1):
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, method="GET")
        resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10)
        body = json.loads(resp.read().decode())
        if resp.getcode() == 200:
            print(json.dumps({{"status": "ready", "attempt": attempt, "body": body}}))
            sys.exit(0)
    except Exception:
        pass
    print(f"Attempt {{attempt}}/{{max_retries}} - not ready, waiting {{interval}}s...")
    time.sleep(interval)

print(json.dumps({{"status": "timeout", "attempts": max_retries}}))
sys.exit(1)

explanation: Python action that repeatedly polls a postgres health endpoint until it returns HTTP 200 or max retries are exhausted.

import urllib.request

import json
import sys

url = "{{input.url}}"
filepath = "{{input.filepath}}"
api_key = "{{input.api_key}}"

if not os.path.isfile(filepath):
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": f"File not found: {{filepath}}"}}))

with open(filepath, "rb") as f:
    data = f.read()

req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="PUT")
req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")
req.add_header("Authorization", "Bearer " + api_key)
try:

    print(json.dumps({{"status": "uploaded", "code": resp.getcode(), "size": len(data)}}))
except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "code": e.code, "message": e.read().decode()}}))

dm_json.code:
import json
import urllib.request
import urllib.parse
import sys

base_url = "{{input.url}}"
max_pages = int("{{input.max_pages}}" or "10")
all_items = []
page = 1

while page <= max_pages:
    params = urllib.parse.urlencode({{"page": page, "per_page": 100}})
    url = f"{{base_url}}?{{params}}"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, method="GET")
    req.add_header("Authorization", "Bearer {{input.api_key}}")
    try:
        resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
        data = json.loads(resp.read().decode())
        items = data if isinstance(data, list) else data.get("items", data.get("results", []))
        if not items:
            break
        all_items.extend(items)
        page += 1
    except Exception as e:
        print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "page": page, "message": str(e)}}))
        sys.exit(1)

print(json.dumps({{"status": "ok", "total_items": len(all_items), "pages_fetched": page - 1}}))

explanation: Python action that fetches paginated results from bitbucket API, collecting all items across multiple pages.

dm_json.code:
import json
import urllib.request
import urllib.parse
import sys

token_url = "{{input.token_url}}"
client_id = "{{input.client_id}}"
client_secret = "{{input.client_secret}}"
refresh_token = "{{input.refresh_token}}"

data = urllib.parse.urlencode({{
    "grant_type": "refresh_token",
    "client_id": client_id,
    "client_secret": client_secret,
    "refresh_token": refresh_token,
}}).encode("utf-8")

req = urllib.request.Request(token_url, data=data, method="POST")
req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
try:
    resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
    tokens = json.loads(resp.read().decode())
    print(json.dumps({{
        "status": "refreshed",
        "access_token": tokens.get("access_token", "")[:10] + "...",
        "expires_in": tokens.get("expires_in"),
    }}))
except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "code": e.code, "message": e.read().decode()}}))
    sys.exit(1)

explanation: Python action that refreshes an OAuth2 access token using a refresh token grant against keycloak token endpoint.

dm_json.name: Dispatch webhook to flux
dm_json.code:
import json
import urllib.request
import hashlib
import hmac
import sys

webhook_url = "{{input.webhook_url}}"
event_type = "{{input.event_type}}"
payload_str = '{{input.payload}}'
secret = "{{input.secret}}"

payload = {{"event": event_type, "data": json.loads(payload_str)}}
body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")

req = urllib.request.Request(webhook_url, data=body, method="POST")
req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
req.add_header("X-Event-Type", event_type)
if secret:
    sig = hmac.new(secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    req.add_header("X-Signature", "sha256=" + sig)

try:
    resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "dispatched", "code": resp.getcode()}}))
except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "code": e.code}}))
    sys.exit(1)

explanation: Python action that dispatches a webhook event to flux with optional HMAC-SHA256 signature verification.

            time.sleep(retry_after)
        else:
            print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "code": e.code}}))

dm_json.code:
import json
import socket
import hashlib
import base64
import os
import sys

host = "{{input.host}}"
port = int("{{input.port}}" or "80")
path = "{{input.path}}" or "/"
timeout = int("{{input.timeout}}" or "10")

ws_key = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(16)).decode()
try:
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    sock.settimeout(timeout)
    sock.connect((host, port))
    handshake = (
        f"GET {{path}} HTTP/1.1\r\n"
        f"Host: {{host}}\r\n"
        f"Upgrade: websocket\r\n"
        f"Connection: Upgrade\r\n"
        f"Sec-WebSocket-Key: {{ws_key}}\r\n"
        f"Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n"
    )
    sock.sendall(handshake.encode())
    resp = sock.recv(4096).decode()
    sock.close()
    if "101" in resp and "Upgrade" in resp:
        print(json.dumps({{"status": "ok", "message": "WebSocket handshake successful"}}))
    else:
        print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": "Handshake failed", "response": resp[:200]}}))
        sys.exit(1)
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

explanation: Python action that tests notifications WebSocket connectivity by performing the HTTP upgrade handshake.

        print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": "Handshake failed", "response": resp[:200]}}))

req = urllib.request.Request(url, method="GET")

    match = actual_version == expected_version
    print(json.dumps({{
        "status": "ok" if match else "mismatch",
        "expected": expected_version,
        "actual": actual_version,
        "match": match,
    }}))
    if not match:
        sys.exit(1)
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))

smtp_host = "{{input.smtp_host}}"
smtp_port = int("{{input.smtp_port}}" or "587")
username = "{{input.username}}"
password = "{{input.password}}"
sender = "{{input.from_addr}}"
recipient = "{{input.to_addr}}"
subject = "{{input.subject}}"
body = "{{input.body}}"

msg["To"] = recipient
msg["Subject"] = subject
msg.attach(MIMEText(body, "plain"))

        server.starttls()
        server.login(username, password)
        server.sendmail(sender, [recipient], msg.as_string())
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "sent", "to": recipient, "subject": subject}}))
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

import json
import urllib.request
import urllib.error
import time
import sys

url = "{{input.url}}"
payload_str = '{{input.payload}}'
max_retries = int("{{input.max_retries}}" or "3")
headers_str = '{{input.headers}}' or "{{}}"

payload = json.loads(payload_str)
headers = json.loads(headers_str)
data = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")

for attempt in range(1, max_retries + 1):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="POST")
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    for k, v in headers.items():
        req.add_header(k, v)
    try:
        resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15)
        code = resp.getcode()
        if code < 300:
            print(json.dumps({{"status": "sent", "code": code, "attempt": attempt}}))
            sys.exit(0)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        if attempt == max_retries:
            print(json.dumps({{"status": "failed", "code": e.code, "attempts": attempt}}))
            sys.exit(1)
    except Exception as e:
        if attempt == max_retries:
            print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e), "attempts": attempt}}))
            sys.exit(1)
    time.sleep(2 ** attempt)

vars_json = '{{input.variables}}'
output_path = "{{input.output_path}}"

def simple_render(template_str, variables):
    """Simple template renderer replacing {{ var }} patterns."""
    def replacer(match):
        key = match.group(1).strip()
        return str(variables.get(key, match.group(0)))
    return re.sub(r"\{\{\s*(\w+)\s*\}\}", replacer, template_str)

try:
    with open(template_path, "r") as f:

    with open(output_path, "w") as f:

import json
import difflib
import sys

file_a = "{{input.file_a}}"
file_b = "{{input.file_b}}"

try:
    with open(file_a, "r") as f:
        lines_a = f.readlines()
    with open(file_b, "r") as f:
        lines_b = f.readlines()

    diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(lines_a, lines_b, fromfile=file_a, tofile=file_b, lineterm=""))
    has_changes = len(diff) > 0
    added = sum(1 for l in diff if l.startswith("+") and not l.startswith("+++"))
    removed = sum(1 for l in diff if l.startswith("-") and not l.startswith("---"))

    print(json.dumps({{
        "status": "changed" if has_changes else "identical",
        "lines_added": added,
        "lines_removed": removed,
        "diff": "\n".join(diff[:50]),
    }}))
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

import os
import re
import json
import sys

input_path = "{{input.input_path}}"
output_path = "{{input.output_path}}"
strict = "{{input.strict}}" == "true"

def expand_env(text, strict_mode):
    missing = []
    def replacer(match):
        var = match.group(1) or match.group(2)
        value = os.environ.get(var)
        if value is None:
            missing.append(var)
            return match.group(0) if not strict_mode else ""
        return value
    expanded = re.sub(r"\$\{{(\w+)\}}|\$(\w+)", replacer, text)
    return expanded, missing

try:
    with open(input_path, "r") as f:
        content = f.read()

    expanded, missing = expand_env(content, strict)

    if strict and missing:
        print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "missing_vars": missing}}))
        sys.exit(1)

    with open(output_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(expanded)

    print(json.dumps({{
        "status": "expanded",
        "output": output_path,
        "missing_vars": missing,
    }}))
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

import json
import sys
import os

threshold = float("{{input.threshold}}" or "80")

def get_cpu_usage():
    with open("/proc/stat", "r") as f:
        line = f.readline()
    parts = line.split()
    idle = int(parts[4])
    total = sum(int(p) for p in parts[1:])
    return idle, total

import time
idle1, total1 = get_cpu_usage()
time.sleep(1)
idle2, total2 = get_cpu_usage()

idle_delta = idle2 - idle1
total_delta = total2 - total1
usage = (1.0 - idle_delta / total_delta) * 100.0 if total_delta > 0 else 0.0
cpu_count = os.cpu_count() or 1

result = {{
    "cpu_percent": round(usage, 2),
    "cpu_count": cpu_count,
    "threshold": threshold,
    "status": "critical" if usage > threshold else "ok",
}}
print(json.dumps(result))
if usage > threshold:
    sys.exit(1)

import json
import sys

device = "{{input.device}}" or "sda"

def read_diskstats(dev):
    with open("/proc/diskstats", "r") as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 14 and parts[2] == dev:
                return {{
                    "reads_completed": int(parts[3]),
                    "reads_merged": int(parts[4]),
                    "sectors_read": int(parts[5]),
                    "read_time_ms": int(parts[6]),
                    "writes_completed": int(parts[7]),
                    "writes_merged": int(parts[8]),
                    "sectors_written": int(parts[9]),
                    "write_time_ms": int(parts[10]),
                    "io_in_progress": int(parts[11]),
                    "io_time_ms": int(parts[12]),
                }}
    return None

stats = read_diskstats(device)
if stats is None:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": f"Device {{device}} not found"}}))
    sys.exit(1)

stats["device"] = device
stats["status"] = "ok"
print(json.dumps(stats))

user_prompt: Create a Python action to check thermal sensors against 85C threshold

dm_json.name: Read temperature sensors
dm_json.code:
import json
import os
import glob
import sys

threshold_c = float("{{input.threshold_c}}" or "85")

sensors = []
thermal_zones = glob.glob("/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp")

for path in sorted(thermal_zones):
    zone = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path))
    type_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path), "type")
    try:
        with open(path, "r") as f:
            temp_mc = int(f.read().strip())
        temp_c = temp_mc / 1000.0
        sensor_type = "unknown"
        if os.path.isfile(type_path):
            with open(type_path, "r") as f:
                sensor_type = f.read().strip()
        sensors.append({{"zone": zone, "type": sensor_type, "temp_c": temp_c}})
    except Exception:
        continue

max_temp = max((s["temp_c"] for s in sensors), default=0.0)
result = {{
    "sensors": sensors,
    "max_temp_c": max_temp,
    "threshold_c": threshold_c,
    "status": "critical" if max_temp > threshold_c else "ok",
}}
print(json.dumps(result))

import json
import re
import os
import sys

log_file = "{{input.log_file}}"

max_lines = int("{{input.max_lines}}" or "1000")

if not os.path.isfile(log_file):
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": f"Log file not found: {{log_file}}"}}))
    sys.exit(1)

try:
    regex = re.compile(pattern)
except re.error as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": f"Invalid regex: {{e}}"}}))
    sys.exit(1)

matches = []
with open(log_file, "r", errors="replace") as f:
    lines = f.readlines()[-max_lines:]
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if regex.search(line):
            matches.append(line.strip())

result = {{
    "status": "ok",
    "log_file": log_file,
    "pattern": pattern,
    "lines_scanned": len(lines),
    "matches_found": len(matches),
    "recent_matches": matches[-20:],
}}
print(json.dumps(result))

import json
import subprocess
import sys

unit = "{{input.unit}}"
since = "{{input.since}}" or "1 hour ago"
priority = "{{input.priority}}" or "err"
max_entries = int("{{input.max_entries}}" or "50")

try:
    cmd = [
        "journalctl", "-u", unit,
        "--since", since,
        "--priority", priority,
        "--no-pager", "-o", "json",
        "-n", str(max_entries),
    ]
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    entries = []
    for line in result.stdout.strip().split("\n"):
        if line.strip():
            try:
                entries.append(json.loads(line))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
    summary = {{
        "status": "ok",
        "unit": unit,
        "since": since,
        "priority": priority,
        "entry_count": len(entries),
        "messages": [e.get("MESSAGE", "") for e in entries[-20:]],
    }}
    print(json.dumps(summary))
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": "journalctl timed out"}}))
    sys.exit(1)
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

priority.description: Minimum priority level (default "err")

import json
import subprocess
import sys

container = "{{input.container_name}}"
cpu_threshold = float("{{input.cpu_threshold}}" or "80")
mem_threshold = float("{{input.mem_threshold}}" or "80")

try:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["docker", "stats", "--no-stream", "--format",
         "{{.CPUPerc}}|{{.MemPerc}}|{{.MemUsage}}|{{.NetIO}}|{{.BlockIO}}|{{.PIDs}}",
         container],
        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": result.stderr.strip()}}))
        sys.exit(1)
    parts = result.stdout.strip().split("|")
    cpu_pct = float(parts[0].strip().rstrip("%"))
    mem_pct = float(parts[1].strip().rstrip("%"))
    status = "ok"
    if cpu_pct > cpu_threshold or mem_pct > mem_threshold:
        status = "warning"
    output = {{
        "status": status,
        "container": container,
        "cpu_percent": cpu_pct,
        "mem_percent": mem_pct,
        "mem_usage": parts[2].strip(),
        "net_io": parts[3].strip(),
        "block_io": parts[4].strip(),
        "pids": parts[5].strip(),
    }}
    print(json.dumps(output))
    if status == "warning":
        sys.exit(1)
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

user_prompt: Create a Python action to test TCP connection latency to database

dm_json.name: Test network latency to database
dm_json.code:
import json
import socket
import time
import sys

host = "{{input.host}}"
port = int("{{input.port}}")
count = int("{{input.count}}" or "5")
threshold_ms = float("{{input.threshold_ms}}" or "100")

latencies = []
failures = 0

for i in range(count):
    try:
        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        sock.settimeout(5)
        start = time.time()
        sock.connect((host, port))
        elapsed_ms = (time.time() - start) * 1000
        sock.close()
        latencies.append(round(elapsed_ms, 2))
    except Exception:
        failures += 1

if not latencies:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": "All connection attempts failed"}}))
    sys.exit(1)

avg = round(sum(latencies) / len(latencies), 2)
result = {{
    "status": "ok" if avg <= threshold_ms else "warning",
    "host": host,
    "port": port,
    "avg_ms": avg,
    "min_ms": min(latencies),
    "max_ms": max(latencies),
    "samples": len(latencies),
    "failures": failures,
    "threshold_ms": threshold_ms,
}}
print(json.dumps(result))
if avg > threshold_ms:
    sys.exit(1)

threshold_ms.description: Max acceptable avg latency in ms (default 100)

explanation: Python action that measures TCP connection latency to a database endpoint over multiple samples and alerts on high latency.

import json
import hashlib
import hmac
import urllib.parse
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone

access_key = "{{input.access_key}}"
secret_key = "{{input.secret_key}}"
bucket = "{{input.bucket}}"
object_key = "{{input.object_key}}"
region = "{{input.region}}" or "us-east-1"
expires = int("{{input.expires}}" or "3600")

now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
datestamp = now.strftime("%Y%m%d")
amz_date = now.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
host = f"{{bucket}}.s3.{{region}}.amazonaws.com"
credential_scope = f"{{datestamp}}/{{region}}/s3/aws4_request"
credential = f"{{access_key}}/{{credential_scope}}"

params = {{
    "X-Amz-Algorithm": "AWS4-HMAC-SHA256",
    "X-Amz-Credential": credential,
    "X-Amz-Date": amz_date,
    "X-Amz-Expires": str(expires),
    "X-Amz-SignedHeaders": "host",
}}
query = urllib.parse.urlencode(params, quote_via=urllib.parse.quote)
url = f"https://{{host}}/{{object_key}}?{{query}}"
print(json.dumps({{"status": "ok", "presigned_url": url, "expires_in": expires}}))

import json
import urllib.request
import sys

health_url = "{{input.health_url}}"
api_key = "{{input.api_key}}" or ""
expected_status = int("{{input.expected_status}}" or "200")

req = urllib.request.Request(health_url, method="GET")
if api_key:
    req.add_header("Authorization", "Bearer " + api_key)
try:
    resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15)
    code = resp.getcode()
    body = resp.read().decode()
    try:
        data = json.loads(body)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        data = body
    healthy = code == expected_status
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "healthy" if healthy else "unhealthy", "code": code, "body": data}}))
    if not healthy:
        sys.exit(1)
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "unreachable", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

import json
import sqlite3
import os
import sys

db_path = "{{input.db_path}}"

if not os.path.isfile(db_path):
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": f"Database not found: {{db_path}}"}}))
    sys.exit(1)

try:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    cursor = conn.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check")
    results = cursor.fetchall()
    conn.close()
    ok = all(row[0] == "ok" for row in results)
    size_bytes = os.path.getsize(db_path)
    print(json.dumps({{
        "status": "ok" if ok else "corrupt",
        "db_path": db_path,
        "size_bytes": size_bytes,
        "integrity": [row[0] for row in results],
    }}))
    if not ok:
        sys.exit(1)
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

import json
import os
import sqlite3
import sys

db_path = "{{input.db_path}}"
migration_dir = "{{input.migration_dir}}"

if not os.path.isdir(migration_dir):
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": f"Migration dir not found: {{migration_dir}}"}}))
    sys.exit(1)

try:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    conn.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (version TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)")
    applied = set(row[0] for row in conn.execute("SELECT version FROM schema_migrations").fetchall())
    scripts = sorted(f for f in os.listdir(migration_dir) if f.endswith(".sql"))
    newly_applied = []
    for script in scripts:
        version = script.split("_")[0] if "_" in script else script
        if version not in applied:
            sql_path = os.path.join(migration_dir, script)
            with open(sql_path, "r") as f:
                sql = f.read()
            conn.executescript(sql)
            conn.execute("INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES (?)", (version,))
            conn.commit()
            newly_applied.append(script)
    conn.close()
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "ok", "applied": newly_applied, "count": len(newly_applied)}}))
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

import json
import socket
import sys

host = "{{input.host}}" or "localhost"
port = int("{{input.port}}")
max_connections = int("{{input.max_connections}}" or "10")
timeout = int("{{input.timeout}}" or "3")

successful = 0
failed = 0
sockets = []

for i in range(max_connections):
    try:
        s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        s.settimeout(timeout)
        s.connect((host, port))
        sockets.append(s)
        successful += 1
    except Exception:
        failed += 1

for s in sockets:
    try:
        s.close()
    except Exception:
        pass

result = {{
    "status": "ok" if failed == 0 else "degraded",
    "host": host,
    "port": port,
    "successful": successful,
    "failed": failed,
    "max_connections": max_connections,
}}
print(json.dumps(result))
if failed > 0:
    sys.exit(1)

import json
import sqlite3
import time
import sys

db_path = "{{input.db_path}}"
query = "{{input.query}}" or "SELECT 1"

except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))

import json
import sqlite3
import os
import sys

db_path = "{{input.db_path}}"
max_size_mb = float("{{input.max_size_mb}}" or "0")

if not os.path.isfile(db_path):
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": f"Database not found: {{db_path}}"}}))
    sys.exit(1)

try:
    size_bytes = os.path.getsize(db_path)
    size_mb = round(size_bytes / (1024 * 1024), 2)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    tables = conn.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'").fetchall()
    table_info = []
    for (tname,) in tables:
        count = conn.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {{tname}}").fetchone()[0]
        table_info.append({{"table": tname, "rows": count}})
    conn.close()
    over_limit = max_size_mb > 0 and size_mb > max_size_mb
    print(json.dumps({{
        "status": "warning" if over_limit else "ok",
        "size_mb": size_mb,
        "size_bytes": size_bytes,
        "tables": table_info,
        "table_count": len(table_info),
    }}))
    if over_limit:
        sys.exit(1)
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

dm_json.code:
import json
import socket
import time
import sys

host = "{{input.host}}" or "localhost"
port = int("{{input.port}}")
interval = int("{{input.interval}}" or "5")
samples = int("{{input.samples}}" or "6")
growth_threshold = int("{{input.growth_threshold}}" or "10")

def count_connections(h, p):
    count = 0
    try:
        with open("/proc/net/tcp", "r") as f:
            for line in f.readlines()[1:]:
                parts = line.split()
                remote_port = int(parts[2].split(":")[1], 16)
                state = parts[3]
                if remote_port == p and state == "01":
                    count += 1
    except Exception:
        pass
    return count

counts = []
for i in range(samples):
    c = count_connections(host, port)
    counts.append(c)
    if i < samples - 1:
        time.sleep(interval)

growth = counts[-1] - counts[0] if len(counts) > 1 else 0
leak_detected = growth >= growth_threshold
result = {{
    "status": "leak_suspected" if leak_detected else "ok",
    "host": host,
    "port": port,
    "samples": counts,
    "growth": growth,
    "growth_threshold": growth_threshold,
    "first_count": counts[0],
    "last_count": counts[-1],
}}
print(json.dumps(result))
if leak_detected:
    sys.exit(1)

growth_threshold.description: Connection growth to flag as leak (default 10)

explanation: Python action that samples redis connection counts over time and alerts if steady growth indicates a connection leak.

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys

file_path = "{{input.file_path}}"
expected_hash = "{{input.expected_hash}}" or ""

if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": f"File not found: {{file_path}}"}}))
    sys.exit(1)

sha256 = hashlib.sha256()
with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
    for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(8192), b""):
        sha256.update(chunk)
computed = sha256.hexdigest()

result = {{"status": "ok", "file": file_path, "sha256": computed, "size_bytes": os.path.getsize(file_path)}}
if expected_hash:
    match = computed == expected_hash.lower()
    result["match"] = match
    result["status"] = "ok" if match else "mismatch"
print(json.dumps(result))
if expected_hash and not match:
    sys.exit(1)

explanation: Python action that computes the SHA256 hash of a backup file and optionally verifies it against an expected value.

import secrets
import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone

key_file = "{{input.key_file}}"
key_length = int("{{input.key_length}}" or "32")
backup = "{{input.backup}}" != "false"

old_key = ""
if os.path.isfile(key_file):
    with open(key_file, "r") as f:
        old_key = f.read().strip()
    if backup:
        ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M%S")
        backup_path = f"{{key_file}}.{{ts}}.bak"
        with open(backup_path, "w") as f:
            f.write(old_key)

new_key = secrets.token_urlsafe(key_length)
with open(key_file, "w") as f:
    f.write(new_key)
os.chmod(key_file, 0o600)

print(json.dumps({{
    "status": "rotated",
    "key_file": key_file,
    "old_key_prefix": old_key[:8] + "..." if old_key else "none",
    "new_key_prefix": new_key[:8] + "...",
}}))

import json
import base64
import sys

token = "{{input.token}}"

parts = token.split(".")
if len(parts) != 3:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": "Invalid JWT format"}}))

    part += "=" * padding
    return json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(part).decode("utf-8"))

    print(json.dumps({{

        "header": header,
        "payload": payload,
        "expired": expired,
    }}))
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))

user_prompt: Create a Python action to check SSL certificate expiry for a api-gateway

dm_json.name: Check SSL cert for api-gateway
dm_json.code:
import ssl
import socket
import json
import sys
from datetime import datetime

hostname = "{{input.hostname}}"
port = int("{{input.port}}" or "443")
warn_days = int("{{input.warn_days}}" or "30")

try:
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
    with socket.create_connection((hostname, port), timeout=10) as sock:
        with ctx.wrap_socket(sock, server_hostname=hostname) as ssock:
            cert = ssock.getpeercert()
    not_after = cert.get("notAfter", "")
    expiry = datetime.strptime(not_after, "%b %d %H:%M:%S %Y %Z")
    days_left = (expiry - datetime.utcnow()).days
    issuer = dict(x[0] for x in cert.get("issuer", []))
    subject = dict(x[0] for x in cert.get("subject", []))
    print(json.dumps({{
        "status": "warning" if days_left < warn_days else "ok",
        "hostname": hostname,
        "issuer": issuer.get("organizationName", "unknown"),
        "subject_cn": subject.get("commonName", "unknown"),
        "expires": not_after,
        "days_left": days_left,
    }}))
    if days_left < warn_days:
        sys.exit(1)
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

import json
import difflib
import sys

current_path = "{{input.current_path}}"
desired_path = "{{input.desired_path}}"

try:
    with open(current_path, "r") as f:
        current = f.readlines()
    with open(desired_path, "r") as f:
        desired = f.readlines()
    diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(current, desired, fromfile="current", tofile="desired", lineterm=""))
    added = sum(1 for l in diff if l.startswith("+") and not l.startswith("+++"))
    removed = sum(1 for l in diff if l.startswith("-") and not l.startswith("---"))
    has_changes = len(diff) > 0
    print(json.dumps({{
        "status": "changed" if has_changes else "identical",
        "lines_added": added,
        "lines_removed": removed,
        "diff_preview": "\n".join(diff[:30]),
    }}))
except Exception as e:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": str(e)}}))
    sys.exit(1)

explanation: Python action that diffs the current postfix configuration against the desired state, reporting changes.

import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone

config_path = "{{input.config_path}}"
backup_dir = "{{input.backup_dir}}" or "/tmp/config_backups"
max_backups = int("{{input.max_backups}}" or "10")

if not os.path.isfile(config_path):
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": f"Config not found: {{config_path}}"}}))
    sys.exit(1)

os.makedirs(backup_dir, exist_ok=True)
ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
filename = os.path.basename(config_path)
backup_path = os.path.join(backup_dir, f"{{filename}}.{{ts}}.bak")
shutil.copy2(config_path, backup_path)

backups = sorted(
    [f for f in os.listdir(backup_dir) if f.startswith(filename) and f.endswith(".bak")],
    reverse=True,
)
removed = []
for old in backups[max_backups:]:
    os.remove(os.path.join(backup_dir, old))
    removed.append(old)

print(json.dumps({{
    "status": "backed_up",
    "source": config_path,
    "backup": backup_path,
    "size_bytes": os.path.getsize(backup_path),
    "pruned": len(removed),
}}))

import json

config_path = "{{input.config_path}}"
backup_dir = "{{input.backup_dir}}" or "/tmp/config_backups"
version = "{{input.version}}" or "latest"

filename = os.path.basename(config_path)
backups = sorted(
    [f for f in os.listdir(backup_dir) if f.startswith(filename) and f.endswith(".bak")],
    reverse=True,
)

if not backups:
    print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": "No backups found"}}))
    sys.exit(1)

if version == "latest":
    restore_file = backups[0]
else:
    restore_file = next((b for b in backups if version in b), None)
    if not restore_file:
        print(json.dumps({{"status": "error", "message": f"Backup version {{version}} not found"}}))
        sys.exit(1)

restore_path = os.path.join(backup_dir, restore_file)
shutil.copy2(restore_path, config_path)

print(json.dumps({{
    "status": "rolled_back",
    "config": config_path,
    "restored_from": restore_file,
    "size_bytes": os.path.getsize(config_path),
}}))

user_prompt: Deploy PgBouncer connection pooler

steps.name: configure-pgbouncer
steps.code:
cat > /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini <<INI
[databases]
{{input.db_name}} = host=127.0.0.1 port=5432 dbname={{input.db_name}}
[pgbouncer]
listen_addr = 127.0.0.1
listen_port = 6432
auth_type = md5
auth_file = /etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt
pool_mode = transaction
max_client_conn = {{input.max_clients}}
default_pool_size = {{input.pool_size}}
INI

steps.name: undo-pgbouncer
steps.code: systemctl stop pgbouncer; apt-get remove -y pgbouncer

explanation: PgBouncer: install, configure pool, write userlist, start, verify connectivity.

user_prompt: Deploy a Flask app with Gunicorn

steps.name: write-gunicorn-conf
steps.code:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gunicorn.service <<SVC
[Unit]
Description=Gunicorn Flask
After=network.target
[Service]
User=www-data
WorkingDirectory={{input.app_dir}}
ExecStart={{input.venv_dir}}/bin/gunicorn -w {{input.workers}} -b 0.0.0.0:8000 wsgi:app
Restart=always
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
SVC

explanation: Flask+Gunicorn: backup, pull, pip install, write systemd unit, start, health check.

user_prompt: Canary deployment on single server

steps.name: deploy-canary
steps.code: cd {{input.app_dir}} && git stash && git pull origin {{input.branch}}

steps.name: route-canary-traffic
steps.code: sed -i "s/server 127.0.0.1:{{input.prod_port}};/server 127.0.0.1:{{input.prod_port}} weight=9;\n    server 127.0.0.1:{{input.canary_port}} weight=1;/" /etc/nginx/conf.d/upstream.conf && nginx -s reload

steps.name: promote-canary
steps.code: systemctl restart app && kill $(lsof -ti:{{input.canary_port}}) 2>/dev/null; sed -i "/weight=/d" /etc/nginx/conf.d/upstream.conf && sed -i "s/server 127.0.0.1:{{input.prod_port}};/server 127.0.0.1:{{input.prod_port}};/" /etc/nginx/conf.d/upstream.conf && nginx -s reload

steps.name: undo-canary
steps.code: kill $(lsof -ti:{{input.canary_port}}) 2>/dev/null; cd {{input.app_dir}} && git stash pop; sed -i "/weight=/d" /etc/nginx/conf.d/upstream.conf && nginx -s reload

steps.code: apt-get install -y apt-transport-https software-properties-common && curl -fsSL https://apt.grafana.com/gpg.key | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/grafana.gpg && echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/grafana.gpg] https://apt.grafana.com stable main" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/grafana.list && apt-get update

steps.name: provision-datasource
steps.code:
cat > /etc/grafana/provisioning/datasources/prometheus.yaml <<DS
apiVersion: 1
datasources:
  - name: Prometheus

    url: http://localhost:9090
    isDefault: true
DS

cat > /etc/grafana/provisioning/datasources/prometheus.yaml <<DS
apiVersion: 1
datasources:
  - name: Prometheus
    type: prometheus
    url: http://localhost:9090
    isDefault: true
DS

steps.name: add-grafana-repo
steps.code: apt-get install -y apt-transport-https software-properties-common && curl -fsSL https://apt.grafana.com/gpg.key | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/grafana.gpg && echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/grafana.gpg] https://apt.grafana.com stable main" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/grafana.list && apt-get update

steps.name: provision-datasource
steps.code:
cat > /etc/grafana/provisioning/datasources/prometheus.yaml <<DS
apiVersion: 1
datasources:
  - name: Prometheus
    type: prometheus
    url: http://localhost:9090
    isDefault: true
DS

filebeat.inputs:

output.elasticsearch:

user_prompt: Create a custom metrics endpoint

dm_json.name: custom-metrics-exporter
dm_json.description: Deploy custom metrics endpoint via script

steps.name: create-metrics-script
steps.code:
cat > /usr/local/bin/custom-metrics.sh <<SCRIPT
#!/bin/bash
while true; do
  LOAD=$(cat /proc/loadavg | awk "{print \$1}")
  DISK=$(df / | awk "NR==2{print \$5}" | tr -d "%")
  MEM=$(free | awk "/Mem:/{printf("%d",\$3/\$2*100)}")
  cat <<METRICS > /var/lib/prometheus/node-exporter/custom.prom
node_custom_load_1m $LOAD
node_custom_disk_pct $DISK
node_custom_mem_pct $MEM
METRICS
  sleep 15
done
SCRIPT
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/custom-metrics.sh

steps.name: create-systemd-unit
steps.code:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/custom-metrics.service <<SVC
[Unit]
Description=Custom Metrics Collector
After=network.target
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/custom-metrics.sh
Restart=always
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
SVC
systemctl daemon-reload

steps.name: undo-custom-metrics
steps.code: systemctl stop custom-metrics; systemctl disable custom-metrics; rm /etc/systemd/system/custom-metrics.service /usr/local/bin/custom-metrics.sh; systemctl daemon-reload

explanation: Custom metrics: create collector script, textfile dir, systemd unit, start, verify prom file.

dm_json.description: Deploy custom metrics endpoint via script

steps.name: create-metrics-script
steps.code:
cat > /usr/local/bin/custom-metrics.sh <<SCRIPT
#!/bin/bash
while true; do
  LOAD=$(cat /proc/loadavg | awk "{print \$1}")
  DISK=$(df / | awk "NR==2{print \$5}" | tr -d "%")
  MEM=$(free | awk "/Mem:/{printf("%d",\$3/\$2*100)}")
  cat <<METRICS > /var/lib/prometheus/node-exporter/custom.prom
node_custom_load_1m $LOAD
node_custom_disk_pct $DISK
node_custom_mem_pct $MEM
METRICS
  sleep 15
done
SCRIPT
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/custom-metrics.sh

steps.name: create-metrics-script
steps.code:
cat > /usr/local/bin/custom-metrics.sh <<SCRIPT
#!/bin/bash
while true; do
  LOAD=$(cat /proc/loadavg | awk "{print \$1}")
  DISK=$(df / | awk "NR==2{print \$5}" | tr -d "%")
  MEM=$(free | awk "/Mem:/{printf("%d",\$3/\$2*100)}")
  cat <<METRICS > /var/lib/prometheus/node-exporter/custom.prom
node_custom_load_1m $LOAD
node_custom_disk_pct $DISK
node_custom_mem_pct $MEM
METRICS
  sleep 15
done
SCRIPT

steps.code:
cat > /usr/local/bin/uptime-check.sh <<SCRIPT
#!/bin/bash
LOGFILE=/var/log/uptime-monitor.log
for URL in {{input.urls}}; do
  STATUS=$(curl -sf -o /dev/null -w "%%{http_code}" --max-time 10 "$URL" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$(date -Iseconds) $URL $STATUS" >> $LOGFILE
  if [ "$STATUS" != "200" ]; then
    echo "ALERT: $URL returned $STATUS" | logger -t uptime-monitor
  fi
done
SCRIPT

cat > /usr/local/bin/uptime-check.sh <<SCRIPT
#!/bin/bash
LOGFILE=/var/log/uptime-monitor.log
for URL in {{input.urls}}; do
  STATUS=$(curl -sf -o /dev/null -w "%%{http_code}" --max-time 10 "$URL" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$(date -Iseconds) $URL $STATUS" >> $LOGFILE
  if [ "$STATUS" != "200" ]; then
    echo "ALERT: $URL returned $STATUS" | logger -t uptime-monitor
  fi
done
SCRIPT

cat > /usr/local/bin/uptime-check.sh <<SCRIPT
#!/bin/bash
LOGFILE=/var/log/uptime-monitor.log
for URL in {{input.urls}}; do
  STATUS=$(curl -sf -o /dev/null -w "%%{http_code}" --max-time 10 "$URL" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$(date -Iseconds) $URL $STATUS" >> $LOGFILE
  if [ "$STATUS" != "200" ]; then
    echo "ALERT: $URL returned $STATUS" | logger -t uptime-monitor
  fi
done

#!/bin/bash
PATTERN="{{input.alert_pattern}}"
LOGFILE="{{input.log_path}}"
ERRORS=$(tail -100 "$LOGFILE" | grep -c "$PATTERN")
if [ "$ERRORS" -gt {{input.threshold}} ]; then
  echo "ALERT: $ERRORS matches for $PATTERN in $LOGFILE" | logger -t log-alert
fi
SCRIPT

steps.name: configure-alertmanager
steps.code:
cat > /etc/prometheus/alertmanager.yml <<AM
route:
  receiver: email-alerts
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
receivers:
  - name: email-alerts
    email_configs:
      - to: "{{input.alert_email}}"
        from: "alertmanager@localhost"
        smarthost: "{{input.smtp_host}}:{{input.smtp_port}}"
AM

steps.name: undo-alertmanager
steps.code: systemctl stop prometheus-alertmanager; apt-get remove -y prometheus-alertmanager

user_prompt: Set up Fail2Ban for SSH protection

steps.name: configure-jail
steps.code:
cat > /etc/fail2ban/jail.local <<JAIL
[DEFAULT]
bantime = {{input.ban_time}}
findtime = 600
maxretry = {{input.max_retry}}
[sshd]
enabled = true
port = ssh
logpath = /var/log/auth.log
JAIL

steps.name: undo-fail2ban
steps.code: systemctl stop fail2ban; apt-get remove -y fail2ban

explanation: Fail2Ban: install, configure jail for SSH, start, verify jail status.

user_prompt: Set up audit logging with auditd

steps.name: install-auditd
steps.code: apt-get update && apt-get install -y auditd audispd-plugins

steps.name: add-file-watch-rules
steps.code:
cat > /etc/audit/rules.d/custom.rules <<RULES
-w /etc/passwd -p wa -k identity
-w /etc/shadow -p wa -k identity
-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k sudo_changes
-w /etc/ssh/sshd_config -p wa -k sshd_config
RULES

steps.name: add-exec-rules
steps.code:
cat >> /etc/audit/rules.d/custom.rules <<RULES
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -k exec_log
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S connect -k network
RULES

explanation: Audit logging: install auditd, add file watch + exec rules, restart, verify loaded rules.

steps.code: grep -q "^PASS_MAX_DAYS.*90" /etc/login.defs && grep -q "^PASS_MIN_DAYS.*7" /etc/login.defs && echo "PASS: password aging" || echo "FAIL: password aging"

steps.name: check-permissions
steps.code: STAT=$(stat -c "%a" /etc/passwd); test "$STAT" = "644" && echo "PASS: /etc/passwd perms" || echo "FAIL: /etc/passwd perms=$STAT"

steps.name: check-no-empty-pass
steps.code: EMPTY=$(awk -F: "($2 == "")" /etc/shadow | wc -l); test "$EMPTY" -eq 0 && echo "PASS: no empty passwords" || echo "FAIL: $EMPTY empty passwords"

steps.name: check-root-path
steps.code: echo "$PATH" | grep -q "\.::" && echo "FAIL: dot in root PATH" || echo "PASS: root PATH clean"

steps.name: check-sshd-config
steps.code: grep -q "^PermitRootLogin no" /etc/ssh/sshd_config && echo "PASS: root login disabled" || echo "FAIL: root login may be enabled"

steps.name: generate-report
steps.code: echo "=== CIS Level 1 Audit Complete ===" && echo "Check syslog for details"

dm_json.name: dkim-signing
dm_json.description: Set up OpenDKIM for email signing

steps.name: install-opendkim
steps.code: apt-get update && apt-get install -y opendkim opendkim-tools

steps.name: configure-opendkim
steps.code:
cat > /etc/opendkim.conf <<DKIM
Syslog yes
Domain {{input.domain}}
Selector {{input.selector}}
KeyFile /etc/opendkim/keys/{{input.domain}}/{{input.selector}}.private
Socket inet:8891@localhost
Canonicalization relaxed/simple
Mode sv
DKIM

steps.name: integrate-postfix
steps.code: postconf -e "milter_default_action = accept" && postconf -e "milter_protocol = 6" && postconf -e "smtpd_milters = inet:localhost:8891" && postconf -e "non_smtpd_milters = inet:localhost:8891"

steps.name: start-opendkim
steps.code: systemctl enable --now opendkim && systemctl restart postfix

steps.name: undo-dkim
steps.code: systemctl stop opendkim; postconf -e "smtpd_milters =" && postconf -e "non_smtpd_milters =" && systemctl restart postfix; apt-get remove -y opendkim opendkim-tools

explanation: DKIM: install OpenDKIM, generate key, configure, integrate with Postfix, start, show DNS record.

cat > /etc/opendkim.conf <<DKIM
Syslog yes
Domain {{input.domain}}

DKIM

steps.name: install-packages

steps.code: echo "A1 LOGOUT" | openssl s_client -connect localhost:993 -quiet 2>/dev/null | grep -q "OK"

explanation: Full mail stack: install all packages, configure Postfix+Dovecot+DKIM in parallel, start all, verify SMTP+IMAP.

dm_json.description: Backup Docker volumes to compressed archive

steps.name: stop-using-containers
steps.code: CONTAINERS=$(docker ps -q --filter volume={{input.volume_name}}); if [ -n "$CONTAINERS" ]; then docker stop $CONTAINERS; echo "$CONTAINERS" > /tmp/vol_backup_containers; fi

steps.name: backup-volume
steps.code: TIMESTAMP=$(date +%%Y%%m%%d%%H%%M%%S) && docker run --rm -v {{input.volume_name}}:/source -v {{input.backup_dir}}:/backup alpine tar czf /backup/{{input.volume_name}}_$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz -C /source .

steps.name: restart-containers
steps.code: if [ -f /tmp/vol_backup_containers ]; then cat /tmp/vol_backup_containers | xargs docker start; rm /tmp/vol_backup_containers; fi

explanation: Volume backup: mkdir, stop containers using volume, tar the volume, restart containers, verify archive.

steps.code: TIMESTAMP=$(date +%%Y%%m%%d%%H%%M%%S) && docker run --rm -v {{input.volume_name}}:/source -v {{input.backup_dir}}:/backup alpine tar czf /backup/{{input.volume_name}}_$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz -C /source .

steps.name: restart-containers
steps.code: if [ -f /tmp/vol_backup_containers ]; then cat /tmp/vol_backup_containers | xargs docker start; rm /tmp/vol_backup_containers; fi

user_prompt: Run a service health sweep

dm_json.name: service-health-check
dm_json.description: Check health of all critical services

steps.name: check-disk-usage
steps.code: CRIT=$(df -h | awk "NR>1 && int(\$5)>90{print \$6,\$5}"); if [ -n "$CRIT" ]; then echo "WARN: High disk usage: $CRIT"; fi; echo "Disk check done"

steps.name: check-load-average
steps.code: CPUS=$(nproc); LOAD=$(awk "{print int(\$1)}" /proc/loadavg); echo "Load: $LOAD / CPUs: $CPUS" && test "$LOAD" -lt "$((CPUS*2))"

explanation: Health sweep: parallel check systemd, disk, memory, load, network, then summary.

  args:
    creates: "/root/.cargo/bin/cargo"
  when: cargo_check.rc != 0

- name: Install {{input.package}} via cargo
  command: "/root/.cargo/bin/cargo install {{input.package}}"
  register: install_result
  environment:
    PATH: "/root/.cargo/bin:{{ ansible_env.PATH }}"

- name: Verify installation
  command: "which {{input.binary_name}}"
  register: binary_check
  changed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "/root/.cargo/bin:{{ ansible_env.PATH }}"

user_prompt: Create an Ansible action to gracefully stop docker

dm_json.name: Gracefully stop docker
dm_json.code:
- name: Check if {{input.service_name}} is running
  command: "systemctl is-active {{input.service_name}}"
  register: is_active
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Gracefully stop {{input.service_name}}
  systemd:
    name: "{{input.service_name}}"
    state: stopped
  when: is_active.rc == 0

- name: Disable {{input.service_name}} on boot
  systemd:
    name: "{{input.service_name}}"
    enabled: no
  when: input.disable_on_boot is defined and input.disable_on_boot == "true"

- name: Verify {{input.service_name}} is stopped
  command: "systemctl is-active {{input.service_name}}"
  register: verify_stopped
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: verify_stopped.rc == 0

service_name.description: Service name to stop

explanation: Ansible action that gracefully stops docker, optionally disables it, and verifies it is no longer running.

user_prompt: Create an Ansible action to set up a systemd timer running *-*-* 00/6:00:00

dm_json.name: Create systemd timer unit
dm_json.code:
- name: Create timer unit for {{input.timer_name}}
  copy:
    dest: "/etc/systemd/system/{{input.timer_name}}.timer"
    content: |
      [Unit]
      Description={{input.description}}

      [Timer]
      OnCalendar={{input.schedule}}
      Persistent=true

      [Install]
      WantedBy=timers.target
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"

- name: Reload systemd daemon
  systemd:
    daemon_reload: yes

- name: Enable and start timer
  systemd:
    name: "{{input.timer_name}}.timer"
    state: started
    enabled: yes

explanation: Ansible action that creates a systemd timer unit with *-*-* 00/6:00:00 schedule, reloads the daemon, and enables the timer.

dm_json.name: Orchestrate app-platform service stack

- name: Stop services in reverse order
  systemd:
    name: "{{ item }}"
    state: stopped
  loop: "{{ (input.service_list | split(',')) | reverse | list }}"
  failed_when: false

- name: Start services in order
  systemd:
    name: "{{ item }}"
    state: started
    enabled: yes
  loop: "{{ input.service_list | split(',') }}"

- name: Verify all services are active
  command: "systemctl is-active {{ item }}"
  loop: "{{ input.service_list | split(',') }}"
  register: service_checks
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: service_checks.rc != 0

dm_json.name: Patch JSON config file
dm_json.code:
- name: Read current {{input.file_path}} content
  slurp:
    src: "{{input.file_path}}"
  register: json_content

- name: Parse and patch JSON
  set_fact:
    json_data: "{{ json_content.content | b64decode | from_json | combine(input.patch_data | from_json, recursive=True) }}"

- name: Write patched JSON to {{input.file_path}}
  copy:
    content: "{{ json_data | to_nice_json }}"
    dest: "{{input.file_path}}"
    backup: yes
    mode: "{{input.mode}}"

- name: Validate JSON syntax
  command: "python3 -c \"import json; json.load(open('{{input.file_path}}')); print('Valid JSON')\""
  register: json_check
  changed_when: false

file_path.description: Path to the JSON file to patch

patch_data.description: JSON string with keys to merge/update

explanation: Ansible action that reads, patches, and writes a tsconfig.json JSON file using recursive merge with backup and validation.

user_prompt: Create an Ansible action to set recursive permissions on a data-directory

dm_json.name: Set recursive permissions on directory
dm_json.code:
- name: Set directory permissions on {{input.path}}
  file:
    path: "{{input.path}}"
    state: directory
    owner: "{{input.owner}}"
    group: "{{input.group}}"
    mode: "{{input.dir_mode}}"

- name: Set file permissions recursively under {{input.path}}
  command: "find {{input.path}} -type f -exec chmod {{input.file_mode}} {} +"
  register: file_perms

- name: Set directory permissions recursively under {{input.path}}
  command: "find {{input.path}} -type d -exec chmod {{input.dir_mode}} {} +"
  register: dir_perms

- name: Set ownership recursively on {{input.path}}
  file:
    path: "{{input.path}}"
    owner: "{{input.owner}}"
    group: "{{input.group}}"
    recurse: yes

explanation: Ansible action that sets different permissions for files and directories recursively within a data-directory with ownership enforcement.

user_prompt: Create an Ansible action to deploy a web docker-compose stack

dm_json.code:

user_prompt: Create an Ansible action to check the health of a worker container

dm_json.name: Check container health
dm_json.code:
- name: Get {{input.container_name}} status
  command: "docker inspect --format='{{.State.Status}}'  {{input.container_name}}"
  register: container_status
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Assert container is running
  assert:
    that:
      - container_status.stdout == "running"
    fail_msg: "Container {{input.container_name}} is {{ container_status.stdout }}"

- name: Check container health
  command: "docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}'  {{input.container_name}}"
  register: health_status
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  when: container_status.stdout == "running"

explanation: Ansible action that checks the running status and health of a worker Docker container using docker inspect.

user_prompt: Create an Ansible action to deploy a api-backend multi-container stack

user_prompt: Create an Ansible action to prune Docker resources on a staging

dm_json.name: Docker system prune
dm_json.code:
- name: Prune stopped containers
  docker_prune:
    containers: yes
    containers_filters:
      until: "{{input.older_than}}"
  register: container_prune

- name: Prune unused images
  docker_prune:
    images: yes
    images_filters:
      dangling: "{{input.dangling_only}}"
  register: image_prune

- name: Prune unused volumes
  docker_prune:
    volumes: yes
  register: volume_prune
  when: input.prune_volumes is defined and input.prune_volumes == "yes"

- name: Prune unused networks
  docker_prune:
    networks: yes
  register: network_prune

- name: Report prune results
  debug:
    msg: "Containers: {{ container_prune.containers_pruned | default(0) }}, Images: {{ image_prune.images_pruned | default(0) }}, Space reclaimed: {{ image_prune.space_reclaimed | default(0) }} bytes"

explanation: Ansible action that prunes unused Docker containers, images, networks, and optionally volumes on staging to reclaim disk space.

user_prompt: Create an Ansible action to initialize a Docker Swarm in production

dm_json.name: Initialize Docker Swarm
dm_json.code:
- name: Check if swarm is already initialized
  command: docker info --format "{{.Swarm.LocalNodeState}}"
  register: swarm_state
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Initialize Docker Swarm
  docker_swarm:
    state: present
    advertise_addr: "{{input.advertise_addr}}"
  register: swarm_init
  when: swarm_state.stdout != "active"

- name: Get swarm join tokens
  command: docker swarm join-token {{ item }} -q
  loop:
    - worker
    - manager
  register: join_tokens
  changed_when: false

- name: Display swarm info
  debug:
    msg: "Swarm initialized. Worker token: {{ join_tokens.results[0].stdout }}, Manager token: {{ join_tokens.results[1].stdout }}"

advertise_addr.description: IP address or interface to advertise to other nodes

explanation: Ansible action that initializes Docker Swarm mode in production and retrieves worker and manager join tokens.

user_prompt: Create an Ansible action to add a database host entry to /etc/hosts

dm_json.name: Manage /etc/hosts entry
dm_json.code:
- name: Add hosts entry for {{input.hostname}}
  lineinfile:
    path: /etc/hosts
    regexp: ".*{{input.hostname}}$"
    line: "{{input.ip_address}}    {{input.hostname}} {{input.alias}}"
    state: present
    backup: yes

- name: Verify DNS resolution
  command: "getent hosts {{input.hostname}}"
  register: dns_check
  changed_when: false

explanation: Ansible action that adds a database hostname entry to /etc/hosts with backup and DNS resolution verification.

user_prompt: Create an Ansible action to configure opendns DNS resolver

dm_json.name: Configure DNS resolver
dm_json.code:
- name: Configure /etc/resolv.conf
  copy:
    dest: /etc/resolv.conf
    content: |
      # Managed by Ansible
      search {{input.search_domain}}
      nameserver {{input.primary_dns}}
      nameserver {{input.secondary_dns}}
      options timeout:2 attempts:3
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"
    backup: yes

- name: Test DNS resolution
  command: "nslookup {{input.test_domain}} {{input.primary_dns}}"
  register: dns_test
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: dns_test.rc != 0

explanation: Ansible action that configures opendns DNS resolver in /etc/resolv.conf with resolution testing.
